Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

clearly adverb

so as to be easily seen, heard or understood

also plainly, distinctly, speak clearly, see clearly, explain clearly

classical

Cic. de Or. 1.144: deinde ut plānē et dīlūcidē
Cic. Phil. 7.17: quī plānē et Latīnē loquuntur

plānē

adverb

plainly, clearly, so as to be understood

Plānē et Latīnē loquī, to speak plainly, without beating about the bush (Lewis & Short). The same word is “quite, completely” (see quite).

Other words

  • clārē — clearly, distinctly (to the eye or the ear); aloud

    adverb · also used · classical · Plaut. Mil. 630: clārē oculīs videō; Ter. And. 754: Dīc clārē.

  • apertē — openly, plainly, without holding back

    adverb · also used · classical · Ter. And. 195: apertē vīs quae restant mē loquī

  • dīlūcidē — lucidly, in a clear order

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.144

  • distīnctē — distinctly, word by word

    adverb · also used · classical · Cic. Leg. 1.36 (Lewis & Short): articulātim distīnctēque dīcere

Examples

  • clārē oculīs videō, pernīx sum manibus, pedibus mōbilis

    my eyes see clearly, my hands are quick, my feet are nimblePlaut. Mil. 630

  • in quā praecipitur prīmum, ut pūrē et Latīnē loquāmur, deinde ut plānē et dīlūcidē

    in which the first rule is that we speak correct Latin, and the next that we speak plainly and clearlyCic. de Or. 1.144

  • Nempe ergō apertē vīs quae restant mē loquī.

    So you want me to say plainly what remains.Ter. And. 195

See also obviously, speak up, quite, unclear.

SourcesLewis & Short: planus · Lewis & Short: clarus · Lewis & Short: aperio · Lewis & Short: dilucide · Lewis & Short: distinguo

Cicero (de Or. 1.144, Phil. 7.17), Plautus (Mil. 630) and Terence (And. 195, 754) checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
